query: We just closed a 12-month deal with a 40-person marketing team. What should the first 90 days look like so they actually stick and renew?
expected_behavior: Frames the renewal as won in onboarding, treating the first 30 to 90 days as the highest-return retention work, not a task to hand to IT
Defines first value in the customer's own terms (a marketing team's outcome like pipeline or campaigns shipped, not seats provisioned or setup completed) and pushes to compress time-to-value
Builds a success plan naming the desired outcome, a dated first-value milestone, owners on both sides, and how both sides know the outcome landed
Separates the required outcome from the appropriate experience, and calls out the sales handoff and closing the promise gap early so it does not surface as a churn reason at renewal
Lays out a 30/60/90 arc (first value, then habit and breadth, then embed and multi-thread) and warns against a feature tour or measuring onboarding by checklist steps instead of value reached
